name: Shemiramoth
overview: Shemiramoth is a male Levite mentioned in the Scriptures as one of the Levites sent by King Jehoshaphat. His role is noted specifically in 2 Chronicles 17:8, highlighting his tribal affiliation and service during that period. Beyond this, no additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemiramoth means 'heights' or 'heavens,' and it may also be a proper name related to a pagan goddess, though this is not confirmed. This name is a proper name and was not given by God according to the biblical record in 2 Chronicles 17:8.
familyAndRelationships: Shemiramoth is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the priestly tribe chosen for service to God. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond this tribal lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Shemiramoth's significance lies in his role as a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat, indicating his participation in the religious reforms and temple service during Jehoshaphat's reign. His mention underscores the importance of Levites in supporting the spiritual leadership and worship practices in Israel. Though not extensively detailed, his inclusion reflects the faithful execution of Levitical duties in a time of revival.
